LESSON: GUIDED READING

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: MANDARIN
Strand: Reading
Topic 2.7: Guided Reading
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Guided Reading, part of Reading in Grade 6 MANDARIN.

Key inquiry question: What strategies can you use to read fluently?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. read the names of body parts (脸、 牙、手、头发) from flashcards in turns,

2. spell out the names of body parts collaboratively,

3. read out items used for self- grooming as peers match them to the appropriate image collaboratively (水、梳子、牙 膏、牙刷、剪刀),

4. read the names of activities related to personal grooming of the body (刷牙、洗脸、洗手、洗澡、梳头 发、编头发、剪头发) ,

5. form simple sentences using acquired vocabulary and read them out for peer feedback,

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. read the names of body parts (脸、 牙、手、头发) from flashcards in turns,
2. spell out the names of body parts collaboratively,
3. read out items used for self- grooming as peers match them to the appropriate image collaboratively (水、梳子、牙 膏、牙刷、剪刀),
4. read the names of activities related to personal grooming of the body (刷牙、洗脸、洗手、洗澡、梳头 发、编头发、剪头发) ,
5. form simple sentences using acquired vocabulary and read them out for peer feedback,

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Guided Reading together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creativity and Imagination: The learner develops networking skills as they discuss and exchange varied perspectives on how

self-grooming builds one's confidence.

• Learning to learn is developed as the learner works collaboratively with peers to match grooming items to their appropriate

images.

Values:
Unity: The learner appreciates efforts of others as they give feedback on the simple sentences constructed on the theme.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Self-management: The learner gains self-awareness on ways of practising good hygiene and grooming to boost their morale.

Link to other learning areas:

The learner is able to relate the concept of personal grooming for overall body wellness to Agriculture and Nutrition.
